statement: Let $ABC$ be a triangle and let $P$ be an interior point such that $\angle BPC = 90^\circ$ and $\angle BAP = \angle BCP$. Let $M$, $N$ be the midpoints of $AC$, $BC$ respectively. Suppose $BP = 2PM$. Prove that $A$, $P$, $N$ are collinear.

Define a sequence $\langle a_n \rangle_{n=1}^{\infty}$ as follows:
\[
a_n = \begin{cases} 0 & \text{if the number of positive divisors of } n \text{ is odd,} \\ 1 & \text{if the number of positive divisors of } n \text{ is even.} \end{cases}
\]
(The positive divisors of $n$ include $1$ as well as $n$.) Let $x = 0.a_1a_2a_3\ldots$ be the real number whose decimal expansion contains $a_n$ in the $n$-th place, $n \geq 1$. Determine, with proof, whether $x$ is rational or irrational.

Find all real numbers $x$ such that
\[
\lfloor x^2 + 2x \rfloor = \lfloor x \rfloor^2 + 2\lfloor x \rfloor.
\]
(Here $\lfloor x \rfloor$ denotes the largest integer not exceeding $x$.)

All the points in the plane are colored using three colors. Prove that there exists a triangle with vertices of the same color such that either it is isosceles or its angles are in geometric progression.

Let $ABC$ be an acute-angled triangle and let $H$ be its orthocentre. Let $h_{\max}$ denote the largest altitude of triangle $ABC$. Prove that:
\[
AH + BH + CH \leq 2h_{\max}.
\]

Let $a, b, c$ be positive real numbers such that $a^3 + b^3 = c^3$. Prove that:
\[
a^2 + b^2 - c^2 > 6(c - a)(c - b).
\]
